entries.name: Thirty men, fifteen to a side

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / The Board and Men / p. 271

entries.evidence: Both figures.

entries.name: The board is two tables, inner and outer

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / The Board and Men / p. 271

entries.evidence: Which table is inner is set by the starting arrangement, not fixed.

entries.name: The starting arrangement of the men

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / The Board and Men / p. 271

entries.evidence: Cannot be evidenced from this corpus.

ambiguity.question: The text says only 'with the men placed as in Fig. 1'. The arrangement is stated in an illustration, not in prose.

entries.note: The rule is fully determined in the corpus -- as an image a plain-text adapter cannot read.

entries.name: Deciding who begins
entries.evidence: Higher single die begins; a tie throws again; repeated ties.

entries.name: The opening thrower may keep the throw or throw again
entries.evidence: Both elections.

entries.name: All subsequent throws use both dice
entries.evidence: That the opening throw is one die and every later throw two.

entries.name: Each die moves one man that many points
entries.evidence: A throw played on one man and on two; the worked 'six trois' example.

entries.name: Doublets are played twice over
entries.evidence: All three worked examples: aces to four points, deuces to eight, threes to twelve.

entries.name: A man may be played only to a permitted point
entries.evidence: Vacant; own men; exactly one adversary man; two or more refused.

entries.name: Two men make a point
entries.evidence: Two men and one.

entries.name: A single man is a blot and may be hit
entries.evidence: A blot hit goes to the bar and restarts from the adversary's inner table, however far advanced.

entries.name: A man on the bar re-enters before any other man moves
entries.evidence: Entry available and unavailable; all other men suspended while one is up.

entries.name: Play is wholly suspended against a full home table
entries.evidence: Six points held by two or more; the adversary throwing and moving alone.

entries.name: The whole throw must be played if it can be
entries.evidence: A throw fully playable, partly playable, and unplayable.

ambiguity.question: An unplayable part is lost and the whole must be played 'if it is possible'. The text does not say what happens when either die alone is playable but not both -- a case every modern ruleset settles explicitly.

entries.name: Bearing off begins when all men are home

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: All fifteen home; fourteen home; a man hit back out mid-bear-off.

entries.name: Each throw may move within the table or remove a man

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: The worked distribution, for both the quatre and the trois.

entries.name: An unusable number bears off from the highest occupied point

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: The six-throw example; and a usable throw, which must be played forward instead.

entries.name: Doublets bear off or move, or both

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: The deuces example: three borne off, the fourth played forward.

entries.name: First to remove all men wins

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: The winning removal, and the loser's state at that moment.

entries.name: A win is a hit, a gammon, or a backgammon

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: All three: adversary bearing off; not yet bearing off; a man up or in the winner's home table.

entries.name: What each result pays

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: Single for a hit, double for a gammon; a backgammon cannot be evidenced.

ambiguity.question: A backgammon pays 'either thrice or four times (as may have been agreed)'. The corpus delegates the figure to the players.

entries.note: Delegated to the players, not to a referee -- the same shape as a regulation delegating judgement to a pilot. An assertion, not a gap.

entries.name: Who throws first in the following game

locator.citation: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 275

entries.evidence: After a hit; after a gammon; after a backgammon.

entries.name: Doubling
entries.evidence: None.
entries.note: Not an omission from the map. This 1909 corpus predates the doubling cube, so the rule is not in it. An engine built from this corpus is a 1909 engine.

entries.name: Opening play advice
entries.evidence: None.
entries.note: Non-normative. Advice, not rules -- but similar advice appears inside the normative sections too ('it is always an object to do this').
